title: Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program Denial Code Matrix and Appeal Windows
content:
A denial on the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program is worked by its denial code, and the code alone decides the route; the self-pay tier has no denials or appeals.

## Matrix by denial code

| Code | Meaning | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| CO-16 | Claim lacks information | Unprocessable and never appealed; cured only by a corrected claim transmitted no later than the tier's corrected claim window in calendar days after the denial's posting date |
| CO-50 | Not medically necessary | Appealable |
| CO-151 | Frequency or quantity not supported | Appealable only when a medical record supporting the quantity, dated on or before the date of service, is on file; otherwise not appealed and handled as a non-covered amount under the program's advance liability notice rules |
| CO-197 | Authorization absent | Appealable only when an authorization grant valid on the date of service is on file; otherwise not appealed and handled as a non-covered amount under the program's advance liability notice rules |
| CO-29 | Timely filing expired | Never appealed and never billed to the customer; Larkfield writes it off with a billing correction adjustment |
| PR-204 | Not covered under the plan | Becomes the customer's responsibility only under the program's advance liability notice rules; otherwise Larkfield absorbs it |

## Appeal levels

**First level.** A first-level appeal may be filed no later than the tier's first-level appeal window in calendar days after the posting date of the denial it appeals, counted in calendar days from that posting date with the last day allowed.

**Upheld decisions.** An appeal decision that upholds the denial posts as a new denial whose original posting is the appeal filing.

**Second level.** A second-level appeal may be filed only against such an upheld first-level decision, no later than the tier's second-level appeal window in calendar days after its posting date; where the second-level window is 0 there is no customer-filed second level on the tier, and on the Medicare Advantage tier the plan forwards an upheld denial to the independent review entity itself.

**One appeal per level.** One appeal is filed per level per denial; a denial already appealed at a level is not appealed again at that level. This is read from the appeals already on file against that denial at that level.

## Appeal window, both sides (hypothetical figures)

| Denial posted | First-level window | Appeal filed | Within the window? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-02-02 | 65 days | 2026-04-08 | Yes — day 65, the last day allowed |
| 2026-02-02 | 65 days | 2026-04-09 | No |

## Points of judgement

- *A CO-197 denial where no authorization grant valid on the date of service is on file.* It is not appealed; it is handled as a non-covered amount under the advance liability notice rules.
- *A CO-151 denial where the supporting medical record is dated after the date of service.* The record does not meet the condition (dated on or before the date of service), so the denial is not appealed and is handled as a non-covered amount under the advance liability notice rules.
- *A CO-50 denial already appealed at the first level.* No second first-level appeal is filed; a second-level appeal is available only against an upheld first-level decision, within the tier's second-level window.
